memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and altar and put up the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard. And so Moses finished the work." - Exod 40:33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"And so Moses finished the work."

The wording is deliberate. When God completed creation, we read that He finished the work He had been doing (Gen 2:2). Now a man finishes a work, and the echo is unmistakable. A new dwelling place has been made.

Look back over what it took. Willing hearts bringing offerings morning after morning. Skilled hands weaving and hammering. Months of labour. Materials counted and recorded. A leader assembling it piece by piece.

And underneath it all, one repeated phrase: as the Lord commanded.

There is deep satisfaction in a finished work done God's way. Not perfection by human standards — completion according to God's instruction.

Most of us live with things unfinished. Half-kept promises, projects abandoned, prayers we stopped praying. Paul was able to say near the end that he had finished the race and kept the faith (2 Tim 4:7). That is worth wanting.

But the completion this chapter really points to came later, outside a city wall, when Jesus said, "It is finished" (John 19:30). Moses finished a tent. Christ finished redemption.

And He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion (Phil 1:6).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God given you to finish that you have left half-done?
2. Are you working God's way or your own?
3. What does it mean to you that Christ's work is finished?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me finish what You have given me, Your way. Thank You that the work of my salvation is already complete. Amen.
